questions.stem: Given the class structure shown below, which types of CIs will be included in a report run against the cmdb_ci_computer table?

options.text: Just CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer
CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all parent classes
CIs defined directly in cmdb_ci_computer and all child classes

questions.explanation: [Platform] CMDB > Table Hierarchy: ServiceNow uses single-table inheritance — querying cmdb_ci_computer returns CIs from the base class AND all child (extended) classes. Parent class records are NOT included; only the selected table and its descendants are returned.

questions.stem: Which field from the configuration item will automatically populate in the Assignment group field of an incident record?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident > CI Integration: The Support group field on a Configuration Item automatically populates the Assignment group field when the CI is selected on an incident. Managed by, Approval group, and Change group fields do not auto-populate the incident Assignment group.

questions.stem: Which of the following are defined for a given change model? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Model (p3083): A change model defines B=State model (states in the model), C=State transition conditions (conditions enabling automatic transitions), and E=State transitions (rules for moving between states). Phase model and phase transitions are not change model components.

questions.stem: When is a change task for Post Implementation Review created for an unauthorized change?

options.text: When the change request moves to Close
When a change manager accepts the change
When the change request moves to a state of Review
When the change request moves to a state of Assess

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Post-Implementation Review (p392): When an unauthorized change is approved, a change task with State=Review and Short Description=Post Implementation Review is automatically created and assigned to the Change Management group. It is not created at Close, Assess, or upon manager acceptance.

questions.stem: Which should be used to explore the entire hierarchy and table definitions of the Configuration Management Database Classes?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CMDB > CI Class Manager: The CI Class Manager provides a visual explorer of the entire CMDB class hierarchy and table definitions, allowing administrators to view, create, and modify CI classes and attributes. Reports, Application Menus, and Dependency View do not provide class hierarchy exploration.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be defined or set through a Catalog UI Policy?

options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views
Setting a catalog category to visible

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog UI Policies: Catalog UI Policies can set variables as mandatory, read-only, or visible/hidden. However, they cannot B=apply requirements to all form views — Catalog UI Policies are scoped to the service catalog/portal experience only, not all platform form views.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item should be used to create an incident record from the portal?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Record Producer: A Record Producer is the catalog item type that allows users to create records in any ServiceNow table (such as Incident) directly from the Service Catalog or portal. Request Items produce sc_req_item records; Order Guides bundle items; Incident Templates are not a catalog item type.

questions.stem: Which incident management roles are activated by installing the ITSM Roles plugin (com.snc.itsm.roles)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > ITSM Roles Plugin (p2557): Installing the ITSM Roles plugin (com.snc.itsm.roles) activates A=sn_incident_read (read access) and D=sn_incident_write (write access) for Incident Management. The roles itsm_incident_read, incident_manager, and itsm_incident_write are not installed by this plugin.

questions.stem:
A customer requests that when the Service Desk agent clicks on the information icon for the Caller's name, the quick view frame shows only the following fields:

User name -

Manager name -

Email Address -

Employee ID -
How would you modify the quick view frame?

options.text: Update the sys_popup view for the user table
Update the sys_quick view for the caller table
Update the sys_popup view for the caller table
Update the sys_quick view for the user table

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Form > Caller Field: The information icon popup on reference fields uses the sys_popup view of the referenced table. Since the Caller field references the sys_user (user) table, update the sys_popup view for the user table to control fields shown in the quick view frame.

questions.stem: Your customer has built a mature knowledge base, with articles targeted to internal audiences -which are technical. Other articles are written for end users, with simple instructions. From the Incident form, the agents would like to be able to identify which articles are visible to the callers What feature would you use, to satisfy this requirement?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Search as User: The Search as User feature enables agents to search knowledge from the perspective of a specific caller, showing only articles visible to that user. This distinguishes internal-only articles from caller-visible articles. Show User Viewable and User Only View are not standard features.

questions.stem: Your customer is using the baseline Create Incident Catalog Item and would like to add a few additional input fields. How should you update the catalog item?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: Catalog Builder is the designated editor for modifying catalog items, including OOTB baseline items like the Create Incident catalog item. Catalog Item Designer is the legacy editor; Item Designer and Form Designer are not applicable catalog item editors.

questions.stem:
Your customer is complaining that Service Desk users keep accidentally assigning Incidents to the Network CAB, instead of Network Support You have confirmed that:
The Network Support group record has the Group types: Incident and Change
The Network CAB group record has the Group type: Change
What could you do on the incident form, for the Assignment Group field, to resolve this issue?

options.text: Add a UI action to hide the Network CAB group from the list
Add a UI action to provide an error message if the Network CAB group is selected
Add Dictionary Override to specify the Incident group Reference Qualifier
Modify the choice list to include only the appropriate group types

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Form > Dictionary Override: A Dictionary Override with a Reference Qualifier on the Incident table's Assignment Group field restricting to group_type='Incident' prevents CAB-only groups from appearing. This is cleaner than UI actions and correct for filtering reference fields.

questions.stem: Which Agent workspace feature gives agents automatic search results that show possible solutions for records they open?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Agent Workspace > Agent Assist (p3157): Agent Assist automatically searches and displays possible solutions — knowledge articles, similar incidents, problems, changes — when agents open a record. Chat Bot, Related Search Results, Knowledge Bases, and Intelligent Agent are not the feature name for this automatic search capability.

questions.stem: Which capability provides visibility to data joined between multiple tables?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Reporting > Database Views (p2215): Database Views provide a virtual join between multiple tables, enabling visibility into combined data from different sources. Metric Tables track performance; Published Reports display existing data; Custom Tables store new data; Breakdown Sources define PA dimensions.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an Incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Resolution: Assignees have two key resolution tools: A=Knowledge Articles (KB accessible from the incident form) and B=Workarounds (communicated from related problems via Communicate Workaround). CI Class Manager, Incident Overview Dashboard, and Enterprise CMDB Dashboard are not direct assignee resolution tools.

questions.stem: When using Inbound Email Actions, what happens if an email is received which has no watermark or reference number?

options.text: New incident created from the message
New interaction is created from the message
Email is rejected and auto-reply sent to sender
New case is created from the message

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Inbound Email Actions: When an email arrives with no watermark or reference number, the default Inbound Email Action creates a new incident from the email content. A watermark/reference identifies existing records to update; without one, a fresh incident is generated.

questions.stem: Under what circumstances, should you use the Communicate workaround Related Link on the Problem record?

options.text: The workaround is helpful information for the Callers on the Problem's related Incidents (open)
The workaround should be published to a knowledge article, visible from the portal
The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Assignment Group
The workaround is helpful information for the members of the Problem's Work notes list

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Workaround (p2858): The Communicate Workaround related link posts the workaround note to all open incidents related to the problem, notifying those incidents' callers. It is not for publishing knowledge articles, notifying the assignment group, or notifying work notes list members.

questions.stem: Which interface is designed for tier 1 IT agents who solve internal or external customer issues?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Operations Workspace (p2943): The IT Service Management Workspace (Service Operations Workspace) is specifically designed for tier 1 IT agents who handle interactions, incidents, and requests. ITSM Dashboard, ITIL Homepage, and Incident Overview are not purpose-built tier-1 agent interfaces.

questions.stem: When using Agent assist in the Agent workspace, what are examples of possible solutions can be automatically searched and displayed? (Choose five.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Agent Workspace > Agent Assist (p2996): Agent Assist automatically searches and displays B=Knowledge articles, D=Problems, E=Changes, F=Cases, and G=Incidents as possible solutions. A=Runbook Actions and C=SQL Queries are not Agent Assist search result types.

questions.stem: Which module is a useful starting point for a manager to view current state operational information for Incident management?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Incident Overview (p2514): The Incident > Overview module provides managers a quick glance at current operational state, with widgets showing open incidents by status (critical, unassigned, overdue). CMDB Health Dashboard focuses on CMDB quality; Critical Incidents Map is not a standard module.

questions.stem: The Problem table is extended from what table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Table Hierarchy: The Problem [problem] table extends the A=Task [task] table, inheriting all task fields and policies (just like Incident). Major Incident, Outage, Problem Task, and Incident are not the parent table for Problem.

questions.stem:
The Problem Manager wants the Problem Coordinators to be able to Re-analyze a Completed Problem.
Which module could they use to make this change?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Problem Properties (p2857): To allow Problem Coordinators to re-analyze completed problems, configure A=Problem Properties (Problem > Administration > Problem Properties), which includes the Re-assess option enabling state reversion. UI Action Groups, State Models, Form Actions, and UI Actions are not where this setting is configured.

questions.stem:
Your Problem Manager has a structured problem management process, which includes a final review of the solution implemented and of the data regarding incident reduction. When a problem is resolved, after implementing a fix, they want the Post Fix Review task to be automatically created and assigned to the Problem assignee.
What feature would you use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Automation: E=Flow Designer automates creation of a Post Fix Review task when a problem is resolved, assigning it to the problem assignee based on field values at state transition. State Model, Workflow Dashboard, Action Modeler, and Task Creator are not ServiceNow tools for this automation.

questions.stem: Your customer needs help defining Category values for the Problem records. What approach should you suggest? (Choose two.)

options.text: Re-use existing categories from legacy systems
Define categories based on the customer’s CMDB classes
Re-use existing categories from incident management
Define categories based on ITIL problem taxonomy

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Categories (p2836): Best practice for defining Problem categories: B=Define categories based on CMDB classes (aligns problem data to CI types for reporting) and C=Re-use existing incident categories (consistency with incident reporting). Legacy system categories and pure ITIL taxonomy are less practical.

questions.stem: When a user clicks on the Communicate fix UI action on the Problem form, what happens?

options.text: Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is On Hold, Awaiting Problem
Fix is written to the Work notes field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active
Fix is written to the Comments field on any Incident associated with the problem, which is Active
Fix is written to a draft Knowledge article

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Fix (p2859): Communicate Fix copies the fix info from Fix notes on the Problem form to the C=Additional Comments (Comments) field on any Active associated Incident. The target field is Comments (not Work notes); the state filter is Active (not On Hold/Awaiting Problem).

questions.stem: Users with which role can Communicate a workaround or fix? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Roles: B=problem_coordinator and D=problem_admin roles can click Communicate Workaround and Communicate Fix on the Problem form. itil_admin is not a standard ServiceNow role; problem_task_analyst is a read/update role without communicate-link permissions.

questions.stem: When a user clicks on the Communicate workaround UI action on the Problem form, what happens?

options.text: Workaround is written to the Comments field on any open Incident associated with the problem
Workaround is written to the Workaround field on any incident associated with the problem
Workaround is written to a draft Knowledge article
Workaround is written to the Work notes field on any open Incident associated with the problem

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Workaround (p2882): Clicking Communicate Workaround copies the workaround to the A=Additional Comments (Comments) field on any open associated Incident. The target field is public-facing Comments (not internal Work notes); the workaround is not written to a Knowledge article or a Workaround field on incidents.

questions.stem:
A tester wants to submit a bug report, because they are not able to see the Communicate Fix link under the Related Links on the Problem form.
What do you recommend that they confirm, before submitting the bug report? (Choose two.)

options.text: Tester is impersonating a user with communications.manager role
Tester is impersonating the assignee, which has the problem_coordinator role
Tester is impersonating a user with problem_coordinator role
The Fix notes field is filled in and saved

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Fix (p2859): Before filing a bug about a missing Communicate Fix link, confirm C=the user has the problem_coordinator role and D=Fix notes is filled in and saved. The link is only visible when Fix notes has content and the user holds the correct role. communications.manager is not a valid role; assignee role alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: Problem and Problem Task records, move automatically from New to Assess states, when which fields are filled? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > State Transitions: Problem and Problem Task records automatically advance from New to Assess when B=State is updated (transition initiated by rule) and C=Assigned to is populated. Short Descriptor and Configuration Item do not directly trigger the automatic New-to-Assess transition.

questions.stem: On a Change Approval Definition record, what does the ‘wait for’ condition define?

options.text: Whether the change approval is sent to an individual user or a group
The state the change must be in before the approval notifications can be sent
The number or percentage of users from the approval group that must approve the change
The fields that must be populated before the approval can be requested

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Approval Definition (p405): The C=wait for condition on a Change Approval Definition specifies the number or percentage of approvers from the group required before the policy is considered approved. Whether individual/group, pre-approval state, field population, and approval sequencing are defined elsewhere in the approval record.

questions.stem: In what table are Change records stored?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Table: Change records are stored in the C=Change Request [change_request] table. change_task stores change tasks; rfc, change, and task_change are not valid ServiceNow table names for change requests.

questions.stem:
Risk is configured by default, to calculate Risk = High for a change that is scheduled with only 3 days lead time. Your customer’s change policy requires that changes be requested with 5 days lead time.
How would you satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Update the Risk Property for Insufficient lead time
Update the Risk Assessment Matrix for Insufficient lead time
Update the Calculate Risk UI Action
Update the Risk Matrix for insufficient lead time
Update the Risk Condition for Insufficient lead time

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Risk Conditions (p457): To change the lead-time threshold from 3 to 5 days, E=update the Risk Condition for Insufficient lead time, which defines the date-based condition triggering high risk. Risk Properties, the Risk Assessment Matrix, the Calculate Risk UI Action, and the Risk Matrix are not where this threshold is configured.

questions.stem: How are Releases related to Projects?

options.text: Project tasks and Release tasks are interchangeable
Projects can be part of one or more releases
Project features are components of a release
Projects need to be completed before releases can be defined
Projects are used to do root cause analysis for releases

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Release Management > Concepts (p2906): B=Projects can be part of one or more releases — a project represents work contributing to a release. Project tasks and release tasks are not interchangeable; project features are not release components; projects do not need to complete before releases are defined; projects are unrelated to release root cause analysis.

questions.stem: What baseline Change Flows support the baseline Normal Change model?

options.text: Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Implement Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Review, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - New, Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Implement, Change - Implementation tasks
Change - Normal - Assess, Change - Normal - Authorize, Change - Normal - Close, Change - Implementation tasks

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Normal Change Flows (p487): Baseline flows for the Normal model are A=Change-Normal-Assess, Change-Normal-Authorize, Change-Normal-Implement, and the Change-Implementation tasks subflow. Normal-New, Normal-Review, Normal-Close, and Normal-Scheduled are not baseline Normal Change flows.

questions.stem: Which of the following Change Task Types are available by default? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Task Types: The three OOTB Change Task types are A=Planning (pre-implementation work), B=Testing (validation activities), and C=Review (post-implementation review). D=Deployment and E=Verification are not included in the baseline change task type choice list.

questions.stem: What is the Business Rule that triggers automatic group assignment on Incident, Problem or Change requests?

options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Auto-Assignment: The A=Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO business rule triggers automatic group assignment on Incident, Problem, and Change by looking up the Support group on the CI, falling back to the Service Offering. The other options are not the correct baseline business rule name.

questions.stem: In the CAB workbench, what are some ways the CAB manager can identify the Change requests to be added to a particular meeting agenda? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change requests meeting different conditions, like Risk level or Type
Change requests planned within a certain date range
Use any of the options on the Agenda Criteria Tab
Change requests for a certain Change Flow Definition

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > CAB Workbench > Agenda (p416): CAB managers add changes to an agenda by A=applying filter conditions (Risk level, Type, etc.) and B=filtering changes planned within a specified date range. These options are available under the Agenda Criteria tab. Change Flow Definition is not a CAB agenda filter.

questions.stem: A change user complains that with the new Preapproved tab, they have to search through many options to find the Reboot Windows Server change. Since they use this change several times per day, it is inconvenient. What should you suggest to make it easier for the change user?

options.text: Drag the change tile to the Navigation pane

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Standard Change Catalog: To quickly access a frequently used standard change, A=use the Pin feature to pin the tile to the top of the Preapproved tab. Favorites apply to navigation menu items; keyword search requires typing each time; change tiles cannot be dragged to the Navigation pane.

questions.stem: Roles control which users can perform which actions on a change record. What are actions, which cannot be performed by anyone, even an administrator? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update Change Type on an existing change record

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Restrictions: A=Updating Change Type on an existing change record (once approvals are generated) and C=deleting a Standard Change Template are system-enforced restrictions no one can bypass, even an administrator. Deleting Change records and CAB Definitions can be done by users with the appropriate roles.

questions.stem: In the baseline Change - Normal model how can Change Tasks be added? (Choose two.)

options.text: Automatically via the Change - Implementation subflow
Manually by the user during New, Assess, and Authorized states
Automatically depending on the category selected on the Change Request
Manually by the user during all states, except Closed or Canceled

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Normal Change Model (p343): Change tasks are added A=automatically via the Change-Implementation subflow (creates implementation/testing tasks) and D=manually by users in any state except Closed or Canceled. Manual addition only in New/Assess/Authorized and category-based automatic creation are not Normal model behaviors.

questions.stem: In the baseline Change - Normal model, when the Change request goes to the Review state, what happens to the implementation and testing tasks, if they have not been closed.

options.text: They are automatically assigned to the Change assignee and closed
An error displays, requiring that the Tasks be closed before moving to Review

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change - Normal Model: When a change request moves to the Review state, any open implementation and testing tasks that have not been closed are automatically canceled. Tasks are not closed, assigned to the assignee, and no error blocks the state transition.

questions.stem: On the Unauthorized Change Properties module what can you configure? (Choose two.)

options.text: Maximum number of unauthorized change records for a CI

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Unauthorized Change Properties (p393): The module allows A=enabling/disabling creation of unauthorized changes when the ci.change.unplanned event fires, and D=configuring CI classes to monitor. Maximum record limits and an Unauthorized Change Dashboard are not configurable from this properties module.

questions.stem: How do you describe the relationship between a Knowledge article and a Knowledge base category?

options.text: Articles can only be published to one category
Articles must be published to at least one category
Articles must be approved by the selected category owner
Articles can be published to a category and subcategory

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Categories: A knowledge article can only be published to one category within a knowledge base. Articles are not required to have a category, category owner approval is not required, and an article cannot belong to both a category and subcategory simultaneously.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can provide feedback on a knowledge article? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Feedback: The four OOTB feedback mechanisms for knowledge articles are B=Comment on Article, C=Helpful? (yes/no), D=Flag Article (flag for issues), and E=5 Star scale. A=10 Star scale does not exist; F=Pin Article is a personal bookmark, not a feedback mechanism.

questions.stem: When using the Knowledge - instant Retire workflow, how does the Valid to date enact a Knowledge article?

options.text: On Valid to date, article is automatically retired
On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge article author
On Valid to date, retire notification is sent to the Knowledge base owner
On Valid to date, the article is archived

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Instant Retire Workflow: In the Knowledge - Instant Retire workflow, the knowledge article is automatically retired when the Valid to date is reached, with no notification or manual step. Other workflows may send notifications first; the Instant Retire workflow acts immediately.

questions.stem:
In the ServiceNow native platform, the service catalog can be accessed via the Self-Service > Service Catalog module. Your customer wants to make modifications to this home page, to add, remove and re-arrange the categories.
Users with what roles can make these edits? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Access Control: The A=catalog_admin and E=admin roles can add, remove, and rearrange categories on the Service Catalog home page. sc_catalog_admin, catalog_editor, and sn_catalog_homepage_write are not valid OOTB role names granting this access.

questions.stem: What would you use to create a New Hire Employee request which would allow you to order your workstation and company mobile?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Order Guide: An Order Guide bundles multiple catalog items into a single request, allowing users to order several related items (e.g. workstation + company mobile) in one submission. A single Catalog Item handles one item type; Record Producers create task records; Knowledge items are informational only.

questions.stem: Which tool allows process owners to use natural language to automate approvals, tasks, notifications and other record operations with little to no code?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Flow Designer: Flow Designer allows process owners to use natural language to automate approvals, tasks, notifications, and record operations with little to no code. Workflow Editor is the legacy alternative; Workflow Mapper, Workflow Manager, Flow Dashboard, and Process Designer are not ServiceNow tools for this purpose.

questions.stem: What process is responsible for defining and managing the lifecycle of all catalog items, by producing and maintaining the services in the catalog and ensuring that a central, accurate, and consistent source of data is provided?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Catalog Management: Service Catalog Management is the ITIL process responsible for defining and managing the lifecycle of all catalog items, producing and maintaining an accurate, consistent service catalog. Service Portfolio Management covers a broader scope; Catalog Item Management and Service Mapping are not standard ITIL processes.

questions.stem:
Your customer needs different catalogs for:
Human Resources - employee facing - for submitting requests to HR
Customer - external customer facing - for ordering company products and services
When these catalogs are created, in which table would the definition be stored?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Tables: Catalog definitions are stored in the B=Catalog [sc_catalog] table. Each catalog (HR, Customer, IT, etc.) is a record in sc_catalog. bs_catalog, sc_portfolio, and sn_offering are not valid ServiceNow table names for catalog storage.

questions.stem: When creating a catalog, which field specifies who can edit, update, and delete catalogs, categories, and catalog items?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Fields: The A=Manager field on a service catalog record specifies who can edit, update, and delete the catalog, its categories, and catalog items. The Editors field controls who can create/modify specific items within the catalog; Contributors, Owner, and Editors serve different catalog administration roles.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: Record Producers are a type of catalog item found in a Service Catalog, used to create records in any table. Requested Items are records generated by ordering a catalog item, not items in the catalog. Categories organize items but are not item types. Execution Plans are not a catalog item type.

questions.stem: Which of the following are users able to do when configuring stages in Flow Designer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Display the stages to the requester
Import a copy of a pre-defined stage set
Define the stage set in a subflow

questions.explanation: [Platform] Flow Designer > Stages: When configuring stages, users can B=create any number of stages and C=import a copy of a pre-defined stage set. Stages can be displayed to requesters but that is a display option, not a configuration action during stage setup; stages cannot be defined within subflows.

questions.stem: When creating a catalog, which field specifies who is able to create, modify, and publish items in the catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Fields: The A=Editors field specifies which users can create, modify, and publish catalog items within that catalog. The Manager field governs overall catalog management; Item Admins, Item Owners, and Authors are not standard Service Catalog field names.

questions.stem: When defining catalog categories and subcategories, what are some good practices to follow? (Choose two.)

options.text: Align categories with CMDB classes where possible
Keep the number of top-level categories to 8-10
Remember that items can only be assigned to one category
Do not go to deep with subcategories: go only 1-2 levels deep

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Best Practices: Good practices include B=keeping top-level categories to 8-10 (preventing choice overload) and D=limiting subcategory depth to 1-2 levels (maintaining navigability). Categories need not align with CMDB classes, and items CAN be assigned to multiple categories — C is factually false.

questions.stem:
In request fulfillment, approvals can be required before a request can be fulfilled. Your customer is worried about requests getting stuck in the process flow, if the approver is on extended absence from the office.
What can you suggest to alleviate this concern? (Choose two.)

options.text: The approver can use the Delegate module to assign a person to approve on their behalf, while they are away from the office
The approver can set their approval notifications to forward to their personal email address
The approval can be defined as a group approval, where any member of the group can approve
The approver can set their approval notifications to auto-reply with “approved” in the subject line

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Request Fulfillment > Approvals: Two strategies prevent stuck approvals when approvers are absent: A=using the Delegate module to temporarily assign approval authority, and C=defining group approvals where any member can approve. Email forwarding (B) and auto-reply tricks (D) are not supported approval mechanisms.

questions.stem: Released in Quebec, what tool enables you to delegate the creation and maintenance of common and simple use case Catalog Items to business users?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: Catalog Builder (released in Quebec) enables business users without admin privileges to create and maintain simple catalog items without technical assistance. Catalog Wizard, Catalog Designer, and Catalog Item Builder are not ServiceNow tools.

questions.stem: Request fulfillment relies on three record types, Requests, Requested Items, and Catalog Tasks. The lifecycle status of these records is reflected in a combination of state and stage fields. Which status field is set by the flow?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Request Fulfillment > Stages: The A=Stage field on the Requested Item is set by the flow (Flow Designer or Workflow), reflecting current fulfillment progress. State fields on Requested Items and Catalog Tasks are managed by business rules and user actions, not the flow directly.

questions.stem:
Your implementation team has a new Business Analyst. They will be attending their first Service Catalog workshop and will be responsible for capturing notes and decisions from the workshop.
What Now Create assets do you recommend they review, to prepare? (Choose two.)

options.text: Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Workshop Preparation Guide
Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Process Guide
IT Service Management - Typical Challenges and Remediation
ITSM - Business Outcomes and Corresponding KPIs

questions.explanation: [Platform] Now Create > Service Catalog Assets: A BA preparing for a Service Catalog workshop should review A=Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Workshop Preparation Guide and B=Service Catalog and Request Mgmt - Process Guide. ITSM Typical Challenges and ITSM KPIs assets are less directly relevant to catalog workshop preparation.

questions.stem: Which role would give you access to the CI Class Manager?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CMDB > CI Class Manager > Access Control: The A=ecmdb_admin (Extended CMDB Admin) role is required to access the CI Class Manager to view and modify the CMDB class hierarchy. ecmdb, class_manager, and sn_class_manager are not valid ServiceNow role names for this purpose.

questions.stem: What module do you use to change the setting for the time between incident Resolution and Closure?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Auto-Close: The D=Incident Properties module (Incident > Administration > Incident Properties) contains settings for resolution-to-closure timing, including the auto-close interval. ITSM Properties, System Settings, Incident Settings, and Resolution Properties are not the correct module names.

questions.stem: By default, when using Inbound actions, what happens if an email is received which has an Incident watermark?

options.text: Incident record is updated, per the action's script
Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat
Incident record is re-set to state = attention required

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Inbound Email: By default, an inbound email with an incident watermark triggers the inbound action script that B=updates the matched Incident record (e.g., adds journal entry, re-opens). The SLA clock is not auto-unpaused; no portal chat auto-reply is sent; state is not reset to "attention required" by default.

questions.stem: When using the Email Client, what is the difference between an Email Template and a Quick Message?

options.text: Email Templates are like forms that can be sent to the caller for completion; Quick Messages are primarily used by the Chat Bot
Email Template is defined and automatically applied when the email form launches; Quick Messages are defined and then can be manually applied by the user
Email Templates are included with ITSM; Quick Messages are new with Machine Learning
Email templates are defined by users with admin role; Quick Messages are defined by users with quick_message_admin role

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Email Client: B=Email Templates are pre-defined and automatically applied when the email form opens; Quick Messages are user-defined snippets manually selected during composition. Templates are not forms for callers; Quick Messages predate Machine Learning; both can be managed by admins, not just separate roles.

questions.stem: Your customer wants incidents to close automatically 7 days after the incident is resolved. How do you meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to trigger from the Resolved date instead of the Updated date
Update the incident_close UI action script
From the Incident Properties application, set Enable auto closure of incidents based on Resolution date to Yes
Modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to expire after 7 days

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Auto-Close (p2473): To auto-close resolved incidents after 7 days: A=modify the Incident Lifecycle flow to trigger from the Resolved date (not Updated date) and C=enable the auto closure of incidents based on Resolution date property in Incident Properties. Modifying the incident_close UI action script and using a duration-based expiry alone are not the correct approach.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an Incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Resolution Assistance: Tools available to assignees to help resolve incidents: A=Known Errors (articles documenting root cause and workaround) and B=Resolutions from similar incidents (Task Intelligence recommendations). CI Class Manager, Incident Overview Dashboard, and Enterprise CMDB Dashboard are management/admin tools, not assignee resolution aids.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to use the Service Catalog to generate task-based records for end-user inquiries. What Service Catalog capability can you use to generate these records?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: D=Record Producers are the catalog item type that generates task-based records (incidents, problems, or any table records) from the Service Catalog. Execution Plans are fulfillment components; Content Items are not a catalog type; standard Catalog Items fulfill requests without generating custom table records directly.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: B=Order Guides are a type of catalog item found in a Service Catalog, bundling multiple related items into one request. Requested Items are records generated after ordering (not items in the catalog); Categories organize the catalog but are not item types; Execution Plans are fulfillment components.

questions.stem: From which table, is the Incident table extended?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Table Hierarchy (p2562): The Incident [incident] table is extended from the A=Task [task] table, inheriting all task fields, rules, and policies. sn_task, Ticket [ticket], and sn_work are not the parent table for the Incident table in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: What optional Incident table is extended from the Task table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Table Hierarchy (p2562): The optional C=Incident Task [incident_task] table is extended from the Task [task] table, inheriting all incident task details. Child Incident, Major Incident [major_incident], and Parent Incident are not separate tables extended from Task in the baseline.

questions.stem: Category and Subcategory values can be set manually on the Incident form. What are disadvantages of this approach? (Choose two.)

options.text: Too many options may confuse users and increase mis-categorization
Choices have no additional metadata to drive process
It is not part of the baseline instance

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Categories: Disadvantages of manually maintained category choice lists: A=too many options confuse users and increase mis-categorization, and B=choices have no metadata (CI class, CMDB data) to drive automated processes. Manually configured categories are part of the baseline instance and are not technically difficult to implement.

questions.stem: When using the baseline business rule, Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO, what behavior would you expect on an Incident form? (Choose two.)

options.text: If selected CI does not have an Owner group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field
If selected CI has a Support group, write that group to the Assignment group field
If selected CI has an Owner group, write that group to the Assignment group field
If selected CI does not have a Support group, write the Support group from the Service Offering to the Assignment group field

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Auto-Assignment: The "Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO" rule: B=if the CI has a Support group, that group is written to Assignment group; D=if the CI has no Support group, the Support group from the Service Offering is used. Owner group is not checked; primary group fallback is not part of this rule.

questions.stem: On an incident record, where are the fields that appear on the caller lookup select box defined?

options.text: The Caller lookup field on the [user] table
The ref_ac_column attribute from the dictionary entry
The ref_contributions attribute on the caller lookup form
The form design of the caller lookup form

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Caller Lookup: The columns shown in the caller reference autocomplete popup are defined by B=the ref_ac_column attribute in the dictionary entry for the Caller field. The [user] table definition, ref_contributions attribute, and form design do not control which columns appear in the autocomplete lookup.

questions.stem: Where do you enable the Search as feature for an incident?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Related Search: The "Search as" feature (showing matching records before creating an incident) is enabled through C=the Related Search Results table configuration, which defines what records appear during the pre-creation search. The incident.deflection property, Incident Properties module, and form design do not enable this feature.

questions.stem: If the Assignment group is empty on an incident record, what happens when an agent that is a member of a single user groups clicks the Assign to me UI action?

options.text: The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group
The Assignment group field is populated with agent’s user group
An error is displayed indicating the Assignment group field must be populated before executing the Assign to me UI action
The Assignment group field remains empty

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Operations Workspace > Assign to Me (p3226): When Assignment group is empty and the agent belongs to only one user group, clicking Assign to me B=automatically populates the Assignment group with the agent's single group. Multi-group members are prompted to select; no error is shown for single-group members; the field is not left empty.

questions.stem: A problem record is the Parent to what record?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Hierarchy: A Problem record is the parent of D=Problem Task records — coordinators create tasks to assign investigation work to subject matter experts. Known Errors are knowledge articles (not child records); Workaround is a field; Major Incidents and Related Incidents are linked records, not parent-child children.

questions.stem:
When you create a problem from an incident, impact, urgency and priority are automatically populated, from the incident record. Your problem management process owner wants the problem manager to be responsible for assessing the impact and urgency on the problem, so they don't want the values from incident to be copied over.
What module would you use to make this adjustment?

options.text: System Policy > Rules > Priority Lookup Rules

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Problem Properties (p2872): To prevent Impact/Urgency/Priority from auto-copying when creating a problem from an incident, configure B=Problem Properties (Problem > Administration > Problem Properties). Priority Lookup Rules handle priority calculation logic; ITSM Properties and Incident Properties do not control this cross-record copy behavior.

questions.stem: As of Quebec, Problem task records will move automatically from one state, to another state, provided the required fields are filled. What are those states?

options.text: On Hold to Work in Progress

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > State Transitions (p2856): Problem Task records automatically advance from C=New to Assess when required fields (such as Assigned to) are populated. Assess-to-Work-in-Progress, On Hold-to-Work-in-Progress, Draft-to-Assess, and Work-in-Progress-to-Closed are not auto-triggered transitions in baseline Problem Management.

questions.stem: A new problem manager wants to know how to create reports for monitoring problem management activities. What do you recommend they do before creating new reports?

options.text: Submit a New Report Request via the service catalog
Take the Performance Analytics fundamentals course
Go to Reports > View/Run > All, then search for Problem reports
Submit a request for the sn_report_creator role

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Reports: Before creating new reports, a new problem manager should C=go to Reports > View/Run > All and search for existing Problem reports to avoid duplication. Submitting a catalog request, taking a PA course, requesting a role, or enabling data collection jobs are not the recommended first steps.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to know why users with the problem_coordinator role can Communicate workarounds, and fixes; but users with problem_task_analyst cannot. How do you explain this?

options.text: The technical resources working on the problem investigation are focused on the technical details, and may provide information that is not useful for the callers
The problem coordinator is the only role with the ability to recall a message
The problem coordinator is responsible for approving or rejecting the proposed message
The message will be automatically displayed on the Portal

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Roles (p2830): problem_coordinator can Communicate workarounds and fixes because A=technical analysts focused on investigation may surface technical details not useful or appropriate for callers; the coordinator ensures actionable communication. Recall capability, approval authority, and portal auto-display are not the design rationale.

questions.stem: A user wants to know what makes the Known Error knowledge base in ServiceNow different from all other knowledge bases. How should you respond?

options.text: The Known Error knowledge base documents problems that are under investigation, but not yet have a root cause
Only users with sn_known_error_write can create Known Error articles
Users with sn_problem_write can create known error articles, but not articles for other knowledge bases
The Known Error knowledge articles use a template, which includes the Workaround and the Cause

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Known Error KB (p2860): The Known Error knowledge base is unique because D=Known Error articles use a dedicated template that includes both the Workaround and the Cause (root cause). Other KBs use general templates; Known Error articles document confirmed root causes, not problems still under investigation; no special write role is required beyond problem management roles.

questions.stem: Problem management provides what benefits for Incident management? (Choose two.)

options.text: Published workarounds help quickly resolve incidents
Problem investigations automatically triggered for multiple user incidents

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management Benefits (p2810): A=solutions implemented through problem resolution reduce future incidents (root cause elimination), and B=published workarounds from problems help agents quickly resolve related incidents. Automatic triggering of investigations and incident manager authorization are not OOTB Problem Management behaviors.

questions.stem: A tester reports a bug, because they submitted a Known Error article from a Problem record, but it is not visible from the Known Error database. What could cause this?

options.text: The article is in draft state, but has not been published
The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated
The user criteria on the knowledge base is incorrect
The tester is not impersonating an itil user

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Known Error Articles (p2871): A Known Error article created from a Problem record starts in draft state and must be reviewed and published before it appears in the Known Error database or search results. It is not automatically published on creation.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the conditions that must be met before a change request can move from one state to another?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Model State Transition Conditions (p352): Change managers define conditions that must be met before a change request can transition between states using A=Model State Transition Conditions. Dictionary Overrides, State choices, and State conditions are not where transition prerequisites are configured.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the interval frequency for unauthorized change detection?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Unauthorized Change Properties (p393): The interval frequency and other detection criteria for unauthorized changes are configured in the C=Unauthorized Change Properties module. Business rules, Event Processing Properties, and unauthorized change flows do not control detection interval frequency.

questions.stem: Prior to Quebec, when you click Change > Create New, which page is displayed?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management (pre-Quebec): Prior to Quebec, clicking Change > Create New displayed the E=Change Interceptor, which prompted users to select a change type. Change Flows and Change Models (Change Landing Page, Change Catalog) were introduced in Quebec to replace the interceptor.

questions.stem: Inside a change flow, you can automate a task with a sequence of related steps, like looking up a record, creating a record, or applying a policy. What is this component of the flow called?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Flow Designer > Flow Actions: In a change flow, A=Flow Actions are reusable components that automate tasks through sequences of related steps such as looking up records, creating records, or applying policies. Flow Activities, Flow Steps, Action Pills, and Flow Tasks are not correct Flow Designer terminology for this component.

questions.stem: On the Release record, what are the available options on the Release phase list?

options.text: Requirement Gathering, Design, Build, Roll-out, Unit Testing, User Acceptance, Pilot
Scoping, Design, Develop, Deployment, Unit Testing, Integration, Pilot
Analyze, Design, Development, Build, Roll-out, QA, User Acceptance
Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, User Acceptance

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Release Management > Release Phases (p2909): The OOTB Release phase list options are D=Requirement Gathering, Design, Development, Build, Deployment, QA, and User Acceptance, reflecting standard waterfall-style release governance phases.

questions.stem: You have created a new Change model and added a new Approval Policy for that model. But the newly defined approval is not triggering. What could cause this issue?

options.text: The business rule "Apply approval policy" on the change_request table has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.
The "Apply Change Approval Policy" action in the flow created for the new change model does not reference the new Approval Policy.
The workflow that triggers the Approval Policy for the new model has not been created using the workflow editor.
The system property "glide.ui.approval.policies" has not been updated to include the new Approval Policy.

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Approval Policies: When using Change Models (Quebec+), approval policies are triggered via the "Apply Change Approval Policy" action in the model's flow. B=If this action doesn't reference the new Approval Policy, it won't trigger. Business rules, system properties, and workflow editor are not used with the new model-based architecture.

questions.stem: In the Quebec release of Change management, what new architectural features were added?

options.text: Change Flows, Change Designer and Change Approval Matrix
Change Models, Change Flows and State Transition Models
Change PIR Assessments, Change Designer and Change Approval Policies

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management Quebec: The Quebec release introduced C=Change Models (fit-for-purpose state models), Change Flows (Flow Designer-based automation), and State Transition Models (condition-based state transitions). Change PIR Assessments and Change Approval Policies came later; Catalog Builder is a different product.

questions.stem: In the baseline implementation, what are key relationships between Change and Configuration Item (CI) records? (Choose three.)

options.text: The CI Manager is part of the change approval workflow
One Change can be submitted for multiple CIs
Changes should reference at least one CI
The CI Support Group is responsible for change implementations
A CI can be affected by a change, even if it is not the CI being changed

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > CI Relationships (p380): B=one change can reference multiple CIs via the Affected CIs list, C=changes should reference at least one CI as best practice, and E=CIs can be listed as affected even if not the primary CI being changed. The CI Manager is not a default approval participant; the CI Support Group manages incidents, not change implementations.

questions.stem: In Change management, what allows customers to define condition based flows for a fit for purpose model?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > State Transition Models (p354): A=State Transition Models allow change managers to define condition-based flows for fit-for-purpose change models, specifying conditions that must be met before a change transitions between states. State Flows, Workflows 2.0, and Conditional Change Models are not ServiceNow terms.

questions.stem: By default, a business rule, causes the Assignment group to be automatically set. How is the group identified?

options.text: Change group on CI record, or if empty, the Change group on the Service offering
Support group on CI record, or the default assignment group for the user
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service offering

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Auto-Assignment: The default business rule identifies the Assignment group by first checking the D=Support group on the CI record, and if empty, using the Support group on the Service offering. Change group is not used for this auto-assignment lookup; the user's default assignment group is not checked.

questions.stem:
Your implementation has some legacy change types with workflows, and also some new change models. What option for Change Create New will support your scenario?
A Change Landing Page
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Interceptor (p338): The C=Change Interceptor is displayed when users click Create New, allowing selection from multiple change types including both legacy workflow-based types and new model-based types. The Change Landing Page (Quebec+) only supports model-based changes; Change Catalog is not a standard option.

questions.stem: Which Change request fields are used in conflict detection? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Conflict Detection (p355): Conflict detection uses B=Planned end date, D=Planned start date, and E=Configuration item to identify scheduling conflicts. CI Business criticality and Risk are not conflict detection fields.

questions.stem: What types of Conflicts are detected automatically on the Change request? (Choose three.)

options.text: Another change for the same CI, at the same time

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Conflict Detection (p3252): Automatically detected conflict types are B=Blackout Schedule conflicts, D=another change for the same CI at the same time (CI Already Scheduled), and E=Maintenance Window conflicts (Not in Maintenance Window). Assignee shift schedules and company holiday schedules are not OOTB conflict detection types.

questions.stem: How are Releases related to Changes?

options.text: Releases are comprised of one or more Changes
Changes are comprised of one or more Releases
Releases are implemented prior to Changes
Changes are implemented prior to Releases

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Release Management: A=Releases are comprised of one or more Changes — a Release represents a set of changes deployed together. Changes are not composed of Releases; the implementation sequence described in options C and D is incorrect.

questions.stem: Which workflow is defined as: Requests approval from a manager of the knowledge base before moving the article to the retired state. The workflow is canceled and the article remains in the published state if any manager rejects the request.
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Retire Workflows: The C=Knowledge - Approval Retire workflow requests approval from a KB manager before retiring; if any manager rejects, the workflow cancels and the article remains published. Knowledge - Instant Retire retires immediately without approval; the other options are not standard knowledge workflow names.

questions.stem: What Knowledge base feature can you use to standardize the sections and fonts on a knowledge article?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Templates: Knowledge article C=Templates allow standardizing the structure, sections, and formatting of articles, ensuring consistent content across the knowledge base. Article designer, Coaching loops, and Article layout are not Knowledge Management features for this purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following roles has the ability to create and manage user criteria for service catalogs?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Roles: The A=catalog_admin role has the ability to create and manage user criteria for service catalogs, controlling who can view or order items. itil_admin, catalog_manager, catalog_criteria_admin, and catalog_criteria_manager are not standard ServiceNow role names.

questions.stem: Which catalog property allows users to save partially-completed requests to complete and submit at a later time?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Properties: The B=Enable wish list property allows users to save catalog items to a wish list for later ordering, saving partially-selected requests to complete and submit later. Edit cart layout modifies the cart UI; Enable cart save and User partial save are not standard ServiceNow catalog property names.

questions.stem: Once a Catalog Item has been requested, what mechanism determines the approvals, and tasks that are triggered in the application?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Request Management (p2916): Once a catalog item is requested, B=Flows (Flow Designer) determine the approvals and tasks triggered during fulfillment. "Request Management allows catalog items to be requested and fulfilled based on defined flows." Processes, Procedures, Actions, and Scripts are not the primary fulfillment mechanism.

questions.stem: Unless there are particular security requirements, what role is given to users that perform request fulfillment work?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Roles: A=itil is the standard role given to users performing request fulfillment work unless specific security requirements apply. itil grants access to create, read, update tasks including catalog tasks. task_worker, sc_fulfiller, catalog_fulfiller, and fulfiller are not standard ServiceNow role names.

questions.stem:
Your customer is a data center. They have a construction department that builds out spaces for new customers. The customer account representatives are responsible for initiating the construction requests. The guidelines are extensive for how to complete the construction request documentation.
Your customer wants the catalog to contain two items:
1. Construction request
2. Getting Started with Construction Requests
The Getting Started Item should contain a link to a Knowledge Article.
What type of item would you use to satisfy the requirement for the Getting Started Item?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: A C=Content Item is used for catalog entries that link to informational content (such as a Knowledge Article) without generating a fulfillment record. Record Producers generate task records; Order Guides bundle items; Catalog Items fulfill requests; Knowledge Items are not a catalog item type.

questions.stem: What is an example of a good use case for an Order Guide?

options.text: Order a case of Laundry Soap

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Order Guide: A=Order a set of Dishes is the best Order Guide use case — an Order Guide bundles multiple related items (starter, main, dessert) into one request. A Custom Automobile, Technical Consultation, Couch, and Laundry Soap are single-item orders that don't benefit from the multi-item bundling an Order Guide provides.

questions.stem: Your customer has a catalog item for Request VPN. They would like to adjust the cart layout for only the VPN item, so the Quantity field is not displayed. How would you meet this requirement?

options.text: On the Cart Layout, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column
On the Catalog Item, Columns tab, unselect Quantity column
On the Catalog Item, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity
On the Catalog, Advanced View, unselect Use cart layout, select No quantity
On the Catalog Item, Cart Layout Related List, set the Quantity record to Inactive

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Cart Layout: To hide the Quantity field for only the VPN catalog item, C=on the Catalog Item Advanced View, unselect "Use cart layout" and select "No quantity." This overrides the global cart layout for just that item. Cart Layout columns, Catalog-level settings, and Cart Layout related lists cannot target a single item.

questions.stem: A manager wants to run a report on the Computer catalog items, to see how many requests are being made for the add on extra memory, as compared with those requiring only the base memory. How would you meet this requirement?

options.text: Build report on SC Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Requested Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Task table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Request table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory
Build report on Catalog Item table, Group by Variables for Computer > Extra memory

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Reporting: To report on variable values (like extra memory add-on), B=build the report on the Requested Item [sc_req_item] table and group by the Computer > Extra memory variable. SC Task, Task, Request, and Catalog Item tables do not contain the variable response data needed for this report.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for an Ask a Question form that would generate an Incident?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: A=Record Producer is the catalog item type used when a form should generate a specific record in any table, such as an Incident. Order Guides bundle items; Linked Items and Content Items are informational; standard Catalog Items generate sc_req_item records, not target-table records directly.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects on the Shopping Cart Widget can be displayed or hidden using Maintain Cart Layouts settings? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Cart Layout: A=Quantity and C=Price are Shopping Cart Widget objects that can be shown or hidden via Maintain Cart Layouts settings. Requested by and Shipping Address are not configurable display/hide options in Cart Layout settings.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants a catalog to contain two items:
1. A request with 1 approval and 2 fulfillment tasks
2. A link to a knowledge article
What type of item would you use to satisfy the requirement for the Construction request?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: A=Catalog Item is used for a request that generates a Request/Requested Item with approvals and fulfillment tasks. Content Items display informational links; Record Producers generate non-request table records; Order Guides bundle multiple items rather than representing a single structured request.

questions.stem: When building multiple catalog items, which components would you evaluate for consolidation and re-use? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Best Practices: A=Sets of Variables (variable sets) can be shared across items with common inputs, and D=Flows and Subflows can be consolidated across items sharing fulfillment logic. Entitlements are not a catalog concept; Icons are per-item assets; approvals are item-specific and not a consolidation target.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for a Computer request?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: B=Catalog Item is the correct type for a Computer request — it generates a Request and Requested Item record and supports fulfillment tasks. Record Producers target custom tables; Content Items are informational; Order Guides bundle multiple items.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can locate items in a service catalog? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the search on catalog or portal
Use the Top Request or Popular Items widget

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Navigation: Users can locate catalog items by A=using the search on the catalog or portal (keyword search) and B=navigating through the category hierarchy. The Top Requests widget is a display feature, not navigation; the Application Navigator is for admin/IT use, not end-user catalog browsing.

questions.stem: Your customer complains that when their users click on the Configuration Item magnifier from the Incident form, that they are overwhelmed by the volume of CIs to choose from. They want to exclude certain types of CIs from the CI lists on the Incident. Problem and Change forms. What do you recommend to your customer?

options.text: Add a Show field to the base cmdb table: Check the Show box on those CI records they want to display; make reference qualifier to display only the CIs with show=true
Use the Principal CI class checkbox, to identify the CI classes that they want visible on the Incident, Problem, and Change forms
Create an Access control to hide the unnecessary CIs from the itil users
Make a show/hide UI action to show only the desired CIs to the itil users

questions.explanation: [Platform] CMDB > Principal CI Class: B=Using the Principal CI class checkbox on CI class records identifies which CI classes are visible on the Incident, Problem, and Change forms' CI reference fields. Adding custom fields, creating ACLs, and using UI actions are not the correct mechanism for filtering CI lookups across ITSM forms.

questions.stem: Incidents are stored in what table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Table (p257): Incidents are stored in the B=Incident [incident] table, which extends Task [task]. sn_task_incident, task_incident, and sn_incident are not valid ServiceNow table names for the incident table.

questions.stem:
Incidents can be created and managed in the workspace, using UI layouts that are tailored to different personas, processes, and interfaces. Examples include:

• Default
• Major incidents
• Self Service
• Mobile

What are these UI layouts called in the Now Platform?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Views: The tailored UI layouts for different personas (Default, Major Incidents, Self Service, Mobile) are called E=Views in the Now Platform. Form Layouts, Workspaces, Forms, and Form Designs are not the correct term for these persona-specific UI layouts.

questions.stem: The Major Incident Management (MIM) application is linked to the Incident management process, but the records have an additional set of States. What are these MI States?

options.text: New, Work in progress, Escalated, Communicated

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Major Incident Management > States (p2500): The additional MI states are A=Proposed (initial candidate state), Accepted (approved as major incident), Rejected (not accepted as major incident), and Cancelled. Reopened, eCAB Convened, and New/Escalated/Communicated are not part of the baseline MIM state model.

questions.stem: What would you use to create Incident records, based on email sent by users or systems?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Email: B=Inbound Flow Actions (Inbound Actions) process incoming emails and create or update Incident records based on the email content and watermarks. Record Producers are catalog-based; Data Collection Jobs are scheduled; Transform Maps handle import sets, not inbound email.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Resolution Assistance: Tools available to assignees: A=Knowledge Articles (searchable KB articles with resolutions) and B=Known Errors (articles with root cause and workaround). CI Class Manager and Enterprise CMDB Dashboard are admin tools; Incident Overview Dashboard is a management reporting tool.

questions.stem: When you activate the ITSM Roles plugin, what additional granular roles are created for the Incident application? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > ITSM Roles Plugin (p2557): Activating the ITSM Roles plugin for Incident Management creates B=sn_incident_read (read-only access) and C=sn_incident_write (create/update access). sn_incident_update, sn_incident_insert, and sn_incident_admin are not roles installed by this plugin.

questions.stem: What are some good practices for guiding your customers' use of Notifications? (Choose three.)

options.text: Make sure Notification requirements and test plans are in the project scope from the start
Get input from Marketing department, regarding format of customer/caller facing notifications
Use templates to ensure consistency and ease of configuration
Use incident.itil.role template as the master template to build all other ITSM templates
When possible, maximize the quantity of email updates to customers

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Notifications > Best Practices: Good notification practices: A=include notification requirements and test plans in project scope from the start, B=get input from stakeholders (Marketing) on customer-facing notification format, and C=use templates for consistency. Using incident.itil.role as master template and maximizing email quantity are not good practices.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to use Incident Tasks on Incident records. But for efficiency reasons, they want to automatically close all Incident Tasks when the parent Incident is closed or canceled. How could you meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: On Incident Properties, for Autoclose Incident Tasks, select Yes
On Incident Properties, for Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled, select Yes

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Properties (p2414): To auto-close Incident Tasks when the parent is closed/canceled, C=select Yes for "Close open Incident Tasks when Incident is closed or canceled" in Incident Properties, which enables D=system property com.snc.incident.incident_task.closure. Options A and B reference incorrect property names.

questions.stem: Incident management includes limited functionality for what advanced reporting capability?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Reporting: Incident Management includes limited OOTB functionality for B=Performance Analytics (PA), enabling trend analysis and KPI tracking over time. Analytics Dashboards are the UI container; Machine Learning Metrics and KPI Reports are not standard ITSM reporting capability names.

questions.stem: Your client indicates they would like a way to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you accomplish this?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > VIP Status (p2457): VIP callers are designated on the incident form using a C=VIP Flag field style, which applies visual highlighting to indicate VIP status in both list view and form. Dictionary entries, Flash action scripts, and Reference decorators are not the mechanism for displaying VIP status.

questions.stem: What happens if an agent hovers over the reference icon next to the caller field on an incident record and there is not a sys_popup view defined for the [sys_user] table?

options.text: The default view of the User form is displayed
Only dot-walked fields will be displayed
There will be no reference icon if there is no sys_popup defined

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Form > Reference Popup: When no sys_popup view is defined for the user table, hovering over the reference icon displays A=the default view of the User form as a fallback. An error is not shown; the reference icon always appears; only dot-walked fields alone are not the fallback behavior.

questions.stem: If the Assignment group is empty on an incident record, what happens when an agent that is a member of multiple user groups clicks the Assign to me UI action?

options.text: An error is displayed indicating the agent must manually assign the incident
The agent is prompted to select the Assignment group
The Assignment group field automatically populates with the agent's primary group
The Assignment group field will not populate

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Operations Workspace > Assign to Me (p3226): When the Assignment group is empty and the agent belongs to multiple groups, clicking Assign to me B=prompts the agent to select which Assignment group to use. The group is not auto-populated with a primary group, and no error is displayed.

questions.stem: Where are the timeframe conditions for sending an SLA breach warning notification defined?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > SLA Management: The timeframe conditions for SLA breach warning notifications (e.g., at 75% elapsed time) are defined in the B=Default SLA flow in Flow Designer, not in the SLA definition record itself. The SLA definition record holds start/pause/stop conditions; SLA Properties and trigger conditions do not contain notification timeframe settings.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to give secure access to business users to view problem records and reports for the products they support. When you install the ITSM roles plugin, what additional problem role is installed to support this requirement?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > ITSM Roles Plugin > Problem Management (p2828): The ITSM Roles - Problem Management plugin installs B=sn_problem_read, granting business users read-only access to problem records and reports. sn_business_user, sn_service_owner, sn_problem_write, and sn_problem_business_user are not roles installed by this plugin.

questions.stem:
A new Problem Coordinator accidentally created several problem investigations that need to be deleted.

What role is required to delete a problem record?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Roles: The D=problem_admin role is required to delete problem records. The itil role allows creating/updating problems; problem_coordinator and problem_manager have operational but not delete permissions; sn_problem_delete is not a valid ServiceNow role.

questions.stem:
A tester has submitted a bug report, because at no point in the Problem lifecycle, does the Create Known Error article link appear under Related Links. Also, they notice there is no Known Error knowledge base in the instance.

What might be the cause of this?
