options.text: The Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin has not been activated
The customer did not pay the bill for Knowledge management
Tester is not impersonating Problem Coordinator
The sn_known_error_write role is required to see the Create Known Error article link
The requirement was not in the stories

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Known Error Articles (p2832): The A=Problem Management Best Practice - Madrid - Knowledge Integration plugin (com.snc.best_practice.problem.madrid.knowledge) must be activated to enable the Create Known Error article link and to create the Known Error knowledge base. Without this plugin, neither feature exists.

questions.stem:
A new problem manager wants a high level view of the activities in problem management.

What module do you recommend?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Overview (p2825): The B=Problem > Overview dashboard provides managers a high-level view of problem management activities, including open problems, overdue items, and trend data. Problem > Homepage, ITIL Manager > Homepage, Process Health Dashboard, and Problem > Dashboard are not the standard module for this purpose.

questions.stem: Why don't Problem records automatically move from Resolved to Closed after the fix is implemented?

options.text: It is designed to follow the ITIL4 standard
There is a scheduled job that automatically moves Resolved problems to Closed after 7 days
There is no Closed state. Problem records are moved to Completed
It is good practice to monitor fixes implemented, to ensure the underlying issues are resolved, before closing a problem record

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Lifecycle: Problem records don't auto-move from Resolved to Closed because D=it is good practice to monitor implemented fixes to ensure underlying issues are truly resolved before formal closure. There is no scheduled auto-close job for problems (unlike incidents); the Closed state exists in the Problem state model.

questions.stem:
In the life of a Problem record, there are opportunities to click the Re-Analyze button and move backwards in the lifecycle.

When you click the Re-Analyze button, what state is set on the problem record?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Re-Analyze: Clicking the Re-Analyze button moves the Problem record to C=Root Cause Analysis state, allowing the team to reopen the investigation. Assess, Draft, and Fix in Progress are not the states set by the Re-Analyze action.

questions.stem:
The key stakeholder for your ITSM implementation wants to have SLAs on every Task record.

What advice do you give regarding SLAs on Problem records?

options.text: SLAs are essential to problem management, as support specialists need to quickly identify root causes
SLAs may be counterproductive to problem management, as the key objective is to permanently fix an error no matter how long that may take
SLAs are available for problem management, but require custom code
SLAs are recommended in the ITIL framework for problem management

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Best Practices: B=SLAs may be counterproductive to problem management because the primary objective is permanently eliminating the root cause, regardless of time. Rushing closure due to SLA pressure could lead to incomplete root cause analysis; ITIL does not recommend SLAs on problem records.

questions.stem: What are two effective measures of performance for the Problem Management process? (Choose two.)

options.text: Problems older than 30 days by Priority and State
Number of Problem that have Breached SLAs
Percentage of Problem Resolution within SLA by Category

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Performance Dashboard (p2886): Effective performance measures include A=Problems older than 30 days by Priority and State (tracking stale open problems) and D=Average Problem Resolution Time (efficiency measure). SLA breach metrics (B, C) are not recommended since SLAs are counterproductive to thorough problem investigation.

questions.stem:
Your customer has an external system, which is used to perform changes. Your customer wants to capture these changes in your instance for reporting and CMDB maintenance purposes.

What baseline Change Model supports this scenario?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Models (p277): The D=Change Registration baseline model is designed to capture and register changes performed in external systems, enabling tracking in ServiceNow for reporting and CMDB maintenance. Cloud Infrastructure, Automated Changes, Retroactive Changes, and Unauthorized Changes serve different scenarios.

questions.stem: Where are the technical approvals defined, that are executed in the Change - Normal - Assess flow?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Approval Policy (p412): Technical approvals executed in the Change - Normal - Assess flow are defined in A=Change Approval Policy records. The flow uses the "Apply Change Approval Policy" action to trigger these approvals. Change Approval Matrix, Assess Approval Subflow, and Change Approval Subflow are not standard ServiceNow components.

questions.stem: What is the trigger for the Change - Normal - Assess Flow?

options.text: A Change request using the Normal Change model is moved to the Assess state
A Change request using the Normal Change model is created
A Change request using the Normal Change model is Low Risk, and is moved to the Assess state
A Change request using the Normal Change model is Assigned to a group

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Flows (p487): The Change - Normal - Assess flow is triggered when A=a Change request using the Normal Change model is moved to the Assess state. Creation, risk level, and assignment do not trigger this specific flow.

questions.stem:
A CAB manager is looking for a way to make their CAB meetings more organized and efficient. They want to be able to:

• Define CAB meeting agendas
• View change calendars
• Review, Approve or Reject changes directly from the change application

What feature would you recommend?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > CAB Workbench (p282): The E=CAB Workbench enables CAB managers to define meeting agendas, view change calendars, and review/approve/reject changes directly from within the change application. CAB Dashboard, CMDB Health Dashboard, CAB Taskboard, and Change Overview do not provide this complete set of capabilities.

questions.stem: What are the Release types available on the baseline release record?

options.text: Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, Patch
Alpha, Beta, Snapshot, Nightly, Milestone, Release Candidate

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Release Management: The baseline release record includes B=Major, Minor, Upgrade, Emergency, Maintenance, and Patch as the available Release type options. Options A, C, and D mix incorrect type names or lists that don't match the OOTB release type choice list.

questions.stem: On a Normal Change Model, what are some examples of the Model State Transitions that are defined for the Authorize state?

options.text: Authorize to Draft, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review
Authorize to Implement, Authorize to Assess, Authorize to Review
Authorize to Canceled, Authorize to New, Authorize to Scheduled
Authorize to Scheduled, Authorize to Closed, Authorize to New

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Normal Change Model: From the Authorize state, the transitions are C=Authorize to Scheduled (approved), Authorize to New (rejected/reverted), and Authorize to Canceled. Transitions to Draft, Assess, Implement, Review, or Closed are not defined from the Authorize state in the Normal model.

questions.stem: What are the components of a Flow Action?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Flow Designer > Flow Actions: A Flow Action has three components: C=Inputs (data provided to the action), Action Steps (the processing logic), and Outputs (data returned). Processes, Subprocesses, and Indexes are not the correct Flow Action component terminology.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Change and Release Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Release management application is required, to use the Change management application
Change includes planning and approvals; Release includes building, testing and execution of changes
A Release can contain one or more Changes
A Change can contain one or more Releases
Change management provides governance, which includes Release management

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Release Management > Concepts (p2906): B=Change includes planning and approvals while Release includes building, testing, and execution; C=a Release can contain one or more Changes; E=Change Management provides governance encompassing Release Management. Release is not required to use Change; Changes do not contain Releases.

questions.stem: In release management, what controls the movement of the state from Scoping to Awaiting Approval?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Release Management > State Transitions: Movement from Scoping to Awaiting Approval in release management is controlled by A=manual state selection — the coordinator explicitly advances the state. Workflows, State Models, and Flows are Change Management mechanisms; Release Management uses manual state progression.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Changes and Incidents? (Choose two.)

options.text: Incidents autoclose upon closure of a related Change
Incidents can be caused by a Change
Incident owners are part of the change approval workflow

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change and Incident Relationship: B=Incidents can be caused by a Change (post-implementation issues) and C=a Change can resolve Incidents (implementing a fix closes related incidents). Incidents do not autoclose upon change closure; incident owners are not standard change approval participants by default.

questions.stem: What are key relationships between Change and Problem records? (Choose two.)

options.text: Changes which cause Incidents, should have an associated Problem
A Problem can be solved by a Change
A Change can cause a Problem
A Problem must be associated with a Change, before it can be closed

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change and Problem Relationship: B=A Problem can be solved by implementing a Change (the fix change resolves the root cause) and C=A Change can cause a Problem (a failed change introduces a new underlying issue). A Problem does not require an associated Change before it can be closed.

questions.stem:
You have just released a new Change Model to the testers. Testers report they can see the old change models, but cannot see the new change model on the change landing page.

What could cause this?

options.text: Testers need itil role to see the change models
New change model needs Active to be set to True
New change models are only visible to Change Managers

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Models: Testers cannot see the new model because B=the Active field on the change model record must be set to True for it to appear on the change landing page. The itil role is not specifically required; new models are not restricted to change managers; publishing a workflow is not the mechanism here.

questions.stem: How are Features related to Products and Releases?

options.text: Emergency releases can include products and features
Products have associated features, which are organized into releases
Features are included in releases, not associated with products
Products use features to define release types

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Release Management > Hierarchy (p2909): B=Products have associated features, which are organized into releases. Features represent units of functionality within a product that are grouped into releases for deployment. Emergency releases do not contain products; features are associated with products; products do not use features to define release types.

questions.stem: When a Service Desk again shares a "How to" item with a customer, what type of record is being shared?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management: When a Service Desk agent shares "How to" information with a customer, they are sharing an A=Knowledge article. Knowledge articles are the record type for informational and how-to content in the ServiceNow knowledge base. Content objects, information items, and how-to documents are not ServiceNow record types.

questions.stem: What are the different ways a user can provide feedback on a knowledge article? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Feedback: The four OOTB feedback mechanisms for knowledge articles are A=Helpful? (yes/no vote), B=Flag Article (flag for issues), C=5 Star scale (rating), and E=Comment on Article (written feedback). D=10 Star scale does not exist; F=Pin Article is a personal bookmark, not a feedback mechanism.

questions.stem: Where should an admin go to view all of the search queries entered by users in the knowledge search?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Search Logs: Admins view all user knowledge search queries in the D=Search logs application, which records every search query entered in the instance. Knowledge queries application, the [kb_view] table, and the [kb_feedback] table are not where knowledge search query logs are found.

questions.stem: Which of the following catalog client script methods will modify the choice list options available to an end user on a catalog item?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Client Scripts: The B=onLoad catalog client script method runs when the catalog item form loads, enabling modification of choice list options before the user sees them. onLaunch, onSubmit, and onSave do not run at form load time when choice list population is needed.

questions.stem: Which property on an order guide will pass variables from one item to another item with equivalent variables?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Order Guide: The B=Cascade Variables property on an Order Guide passes variable values from one included item to equivalent variables in other included items, reducing duplicate entry. Waterfall Variables, Share Variables, and Mirror Variables are not valid ServiceNow Order Guide property names.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow contains a resource with information about all services. It is used to support the sale and delivery of services to employees and customers. It includes information about deliverables, options, prices, delivery and performance targets.

What is this resource called?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Catalog: The E=Service Catalog is the ServiceNow resource containing all available services with information about deliverables, options, prices, and delivery/performance targets. Service Portal is the access interface; Service Dashboard is a reporting tool; Service Map visualizes CI relationships; Service One Stop Shop is not a ServiceNow concept.

questions.stem: The ability to authorize requests is enabled using a role which requires a user license. What is this role?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Approvals: The A=approver_user role enables users to authorize requests and requires a named user license. sn_approval_write, sc_approver, and approver are not standard ServiceNow role names for request authorization.

questions.stem: Released in Quebec, what tool enables the creation of templates for Catalog Items?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: D=Catalog Builder, released in Quebec, enables business users without admin privileges to create and maintain catalog item templates. Template Builder, Catalog Wizard, Catalog Template Library, and Template Management are not ServiceNow-named tools.

questions.stem:
Your customer would like to add a field to the Something is Broken record producer form.

Which formatter would you use to add the field?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Record Producers: To add a field (variable) to a Record Producer form, use the C=Default Variables Editor formatter embedded on the record producer. Record producers use variables, not native form fields; the Default Variables Editor is the interface for adding/configuring variables. Form Designer and Variable Designer are not the correct tools for this.

questions.stem: Which record type would you use for a View Company Policies link that would redirect to a Knowledge Article?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: C=Content Item is the catalog item type for a link redirecting to a Knowledge Article or external URL, with no fulfillment record generated. Knowledge Item is not a catalog type; Record Producers create task records; Order Guides bundle items; Catalog Items generate Requested Item records.

questions.stem:
On a request form, the requester needs to indicate when they need to receive the item.

What Variable type would you use for this information?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Variable Types: A=Date is the variable type for a requester to specify a specific calendar date (e.g., needed-by date). Due Date and Duration are not standard ServiceNow catalog variable types; Date Picker is not a separate type — Date renders as a date picker.

questions.stem: Which type of catalog item may be found in a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Item Types: B=Content Items (informational links to Knowledge Articles or external URLs) are a catalog item type found in the Service Catalog. Requested Items are fulfillment records generated after ordering; Categories organize the catalog; Execution Plans are fulfillment mechanisms, not catalog item types.

questions.stem: When a user submits a service request from a catalog, what actions are triggered, based on the flow definition? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Request Fulfillment: When a catalog request is submitted, the flow definition triggers A=Tasks (catalog tasks assigned to fulfillers), D=Notifications (to callers and fulfillment teams), and E=Approvals (approval records for designated approvers). Access Controls are security configuration; Action Specs is not a valid flow-triggered item type.

questions.stem: When building out a service catalog, categorizing items helps users navigate and search in the catalog. Which roles would allow you to create and maintain categories? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Roles: Creating and maintaining catalog categories requires A=catalog_admin (full catalog admin), C=catalog_manager (manages catalog content), or D=catalog_editor (edits items and categories). itil_admin and catalog_builder_editor do not grant category creation/maintenance rights.

questions.stem: When defining SLAs for the service catalog, at what level is the SLA typically defined?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > SLA Management: SLAs for service catalog fulfillment are typically defined at the A=Requested Item (sc_req_item) level, tracking fulfillment time per item. The Request level is too broad; Catalog Task is too granular; Service Catalog level is not where item-specific SLAs are defined.

questions.stem: What functionality can be used to define the sequence of activities that should be taken to complete catalog items? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Fulfillment: The sequence of activities for completing catalog items can be defined using B=Workflow (legacy workflow engine) or D=Flow (Flow Designer, the modern approach). Activity Map is not a ServiceNow term; State Transitions alone are not a fulfillment sequencing mechanism.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to limit the users who are able to see internal Network requests, to members of the Network department.

Which roles would enable you to make these required changes? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Access Control: Restricting catalog item visibility requires B=user_criteria_admin (creates and manages user criteria defining who can access items) and C=catalog_admin (applies user criteria to catalog items). catalog_editor and catalog_manager cannot manage user criteria.

questions.stem: What should you use to capture data in a grid layout on a catalog item?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Variables: The A=Multi-row variable set captures data in a grid/table layout, allowing users to enter multiple rows of structured data on a catalog item. A standard Variable set is a flat grouping; Cascade variable and Grid variable are not ServiceNow variable types.

questions.stem: From a data model perspective, which table is the base class for the configuration management database?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CMDB > Data Model: The D=Base Configuration Item [cmdb] table is the root base class for the CMDB. The Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] table extends cmdb and is the parent of most CI classes; Asset [asset] is a separate table; Base Item [cmdb_base_item] is not a standard CMDB table name.

questions.stem: Which role has the ability to configure and manage Incident Management properties?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Roles: The D=incident_manager role has the ability to configure and manage Incident Management properties. The itil role can manage incidents but not properties; incident_admin is not a standard ServiceNow role; itil_admin is broader but incident_manager is the specific role for incident property configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following options can a survey administrator define on an individual survey? (Choose two.)

options.text: The ability for end users to decline survey assignments

questions.explanation: [Platform] Surveys: A survey administrator can define C=trigger conditions (determining when surveys are automatically sent) and D=anonymize responses (keeping responses anonymous). The ability to decline assignments and number of reminder notifications are not typically per-survey configuration options.

questions.stem: How do you define the content that is tracked and displayed in all Incident record activity streams?

options.text: Configure the Activity stream client script
Configure the dictionary entry for the Activity stream
Configure the available fields from the Activity stream filter

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Activity Stream: The content tracked and displayed in Incident activity streams is configured through D=the available fields in the Activity stream filter. Client scripts, form design, and dictionary entries do not control activity stream field visibility.

questions.stem: Which table stores incident categories and subcategories?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Categories: Incident categories and subcategories are stored as choice list values in the C=Choice [sys_choice] table, with the table name pointing to the incident table. sys_category, task_category, and the incident table itself do not store these category definitions.

questions.stem: What is normally done when a Root Cause and a Workaround are identified for a problem to document the quickest known resolution?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Known Error Articles (p2860): When both a root cause and a workaround are identified, B=Document a Known Error is the correct action — a Known Error article documents both the root cause and the workaround as the quickest known resolution. A Known Error is specifically defined as a problem whose root cause and workaround are both known.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants Problem records to be assigned automatically to the Support group associated with the CI on the problem record.

Which business rule already satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO
Populate Assignment Group based on Cl Support Group
Problem Assignment Group based on CI Support Group

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Auto-Assignment: The A=Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO business rule automatically assigns Problem records to the Support group on the CI record, falling back to the Service Offering if the CI support group is empty. The other options are not valid business rule names.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to change the way Priority on Problem records is calculated based on Impact and Urgency.

Which module should you use to locate and update the Priority Problem Lookup record?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Priority (p2872): Priority on Problem records is calculated using Data Lookup rules. The C=Data Lookup Definitions module is where you locate and update the Priority Problem Lookup record. Priority Matrix, Choice Lists, and Priority Rule Definitions are not where these data lookup rules are managed.

questions.stem:
The current status of a problem record is tracked in the State field. Each state has a label, value and constant. This example is for Fix in Progress state:


Label: Fix in Progress -

Value: 104 -
Constant Problem State STATES.FIX IN PROGRESS

Your customer wants to add a prerequisite for moving out of the Fix in Progress state. When you update the script include which value is better to use in the script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Scripting: C=ProblemState.STATES.FIX_IN_PROGRESS is the preferred constant in scripts for the Fix in Progress state. It is more maintainable than hard-coding integer 104, avoids magic numbers, and clearly communicates intent. String literals and composite values are not valid or recommended.

questions.stem:
A problem investigation had been previously closed, because the risk was accepted, in favor of using the workaround, instead of applying the fix. After a couple of weeks, the issue starts to occur more frequently, so management wants to re-visit the root cause analysis.

What would be the next step for this problem?

options.text: If 7 days has passed, since the Problem was closed, it cannot be re-opened
Problem Manager clicks Re-Analyze on the Problem record
Problem Assignee clicks Re-Open on the Problem record
Administrator clicks Re-Open on the Problem Record

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Problem Management > Re-Analyze: When a previously closed problem resurfaces, B=the Problem Manager clicks Re-Analyze on the Problem record, moving it back to Root Cause Analysis state. Problems can be reopened regardless of age; Re-Open is not the button used; only problem_manager/admin can perform this action.

questions.stem: Which baseline Change Flow automatically generates a Change task, for Post Implementation Review?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Flows (p487): The A=Change - Emergency - Review flow automatically generates a Change task for Post Implementation Review when processing emergency changes in the review state. Authorize and Implement flows are for different phases; Change - Emergency - PIR is not a standard baseline flow.

questions.stem:
Your customer wants to use the Normal change model, but wants to add another level of approval for changes relating to the Service, SAP Enterprise Services.

What should you do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Add a new Policy Input to the Normal Change Approval Policy
Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Approval Policy
Add a new Change Approval Policy
Add a new Decision to the Normal Change Workflow

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Approval Policy (p413): To add conditional approvals for specific services, B=add a new Decision to the existing Normal Change Approval Policy with a condition matching SAP Enterprise Services. A single policy can contain multiple decisions for different scenarios; a new separate policy adds unnecessary complexity.

questions.stem: What actions can a user with the itil_admin role take in support of Change Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Roles: The itil_admin role supports A=managing Risk Assessments, C=managing Risk Conditions, and D=deleting Change records. B=Deleting CAB Definitions requires change_manager; E=creating and managing Approval Policies requires change_manager or admin role.

questions.stem:
You have just upgraded your instance and have not migrated to multimodal change.

Using the default settings, when you click on Change > Create new, what page displays?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management: After an upgrade without migration to multimodal change, clicking Change > Create New displays the A=Change Interceptor (pre-Quebec mechanism for selecting change types). The Change Landing Page only appears after migrating to the new multimodal change architecture.

questions.stem: What is an example of a Key Performance Indicator for Change management that is included with Performance Analytics, but not available in ServiceNow reporting? (Choose two.)

options.text: Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Change Type
Count of Completed Changes per Month, by Category

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Performance Analytics (p370): A=% Successful Changes and C=% Unauthorized Changes are PA KPIs requiring Performance Analytics indicator calculations, not available in standard ServiceNow reporting. Count-based metrics by type or category (B, D) can be generated using standard reports.

questions.stem: Your customer wants to add a notification to the Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow. What is the first thing you would do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Create a copy of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and then edit the new copy
Create a backup of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, and edit the baseline flow
Deactivate the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow
Unpublish the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Flows: A=Create a copy of the baseline Change - Emergency - Authorize Flow, then edit the copy. Best practice requires never modifying baseline flows directly; cloning preserves the original. Creating a backup and editing the baseline, deactivating, or unpublishing the baseline are not the recommended first steps.

questions.stem: In Change Management, what does a Model State contain? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Models (p3083): A Model State contains A=Model State Transition Conditions (conditions that must be met for a transition) and D=Model State Transitions (the from/to state relationships). Model State Properties and Model State Transition Policies are not standard components of a Model State record.

questions.stem: At which level can the type of knowledge feedback be enabled or disabled?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Knowledge Management > Feedback: The type of knowledge feedback enabled or disabled (Helpful?, Flag, Star rating, Comments) is configured at the A=Knowledge base level. Individual articles, categories, and article templates do not have independent feedback type enable/disable settings.

questions.stem:
A customer wants to add a new Catalog Item to the Service Catalog.

What process would be used to ensure the new item is authorized?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management: Adding a new Catalog Item to a production Service Catalog is a change to the IT service environment, so D=Change Management is the process used to authorize the change before it is deployed. Fulfillment Management, Release Management, Configuration Management, and Catalog Management are not the authorization process for new catalog items.

questions.stem: Which of the following cannot be defined or set through a Catalog UI Policy?

options.text: Apply a requirement to all form views
Reverse UI Policy if conditions are false

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog UI Policies: A=Applying a policy to all form views is not possible with Catalog UI Policies — they are view-specific. Catalog UI Policies can B=set a variable to mandatory, C=reverse if conditions are false, and D=set a variable to read-only. Global view application is a standard UI Policy capability not available in Catalog UI Policies.

questions.stem: When configuring stages in Flow Designer, what are some of the options that can be done? (Choose two.)

options.text: Stage labels and names can be changed
States for the requested item records can be renamed
Define a Service Level Agreement for a stage

questions.explanation: [Platform] Flow Designer > Stages: When configuring stages, A=stage labels and names can be changed (customized display text) and D=estimated durations can be set per stage. Renaming sc_req_item state values and defining SLAs at the stage level are not available in Flow Designer stage configuration.

questions.stem: How are Service Catalogs and Catalog Items related? (Choose two.)

options.text: A catalog item can be associated with one or more service catalogs
Access to catalog items is determined by the service catalog's assigned user criteria
Service catalogs may contain multiple catalog items
A catalog item can only be associated with one service catalog

questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Structure: A=A catalog item can be associated with one or more service catalogs (not limited to one) and C=service catalogs may contain multiple catalog items. D is incorrect because items can belong to multiple catalogs; access is determined by user criteria on the item, not solely the catalog.

questions.stem: Which role has the ability to modify the cart layout?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Cart Layout: C=catalog_admin role has the ability to modify cart layouts in the Service Catalog. itil and itil_admin roles are ITSM operational roles without catalog admin rights; catalog_manager can manage content but not cart layout configuration.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements are automatically included in the name of the update set for items published via Catalog Builder? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: Update set names generated by Catalog Builder automatically include B=item name and E=timestamp. The catalog name, variable details, and item author are not automatically included in the update set name.

questions.stem: What would you use to define a common grouping of configuration items such as all web servers in Miami?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > CI Groups (p382): A D=Dynamic CI group defines a common grouping of CIs using filter conditions (e.g., all web servers in Miami), dynamically including matching CIs. CI class is a classification; Dependent group and CSDM component group are not mechanisms for grouping CIs by location or type in this context.

questions.stem: After publishing an Item via Catalog Builder, the associated update set is set to which state?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: After publishing an item via Catalog Builder, the associated update set is automatically set to B=Complete state, making it ready for promotion to other instances. In progress is the working state; New is the initial state; Published is not a valid update set state.

questions.stem: Which platform role can create service portfolios and taxonomy nodes?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Roles (p3464): The B=portfolio_admin role can create service portfolios and taxonomy nodes, as well as edit, delete, and manage all portfolio components. portfolio_viewer has read-only access; portfolio_manager is not a standard SPM role; portfolio_editor can edit but not create portfolios.

questions.stem: Which of these can be associated with a service within the service portfolio taxonomy?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Taxonomy (p3431): Services are associated with D=Leaf nodes in the portfolio taxonomy hierarchy. A leaf node is the terminal node in the taxonomy structure to which actual services are attached. Node layer, Node (taxonomy node), and Node level describe structural elements, not the specific point of service association.

questions.stem: Which service types can be managed through the scope of Service Portfolio Management? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Service Types (p3441): SPM manages B=Technical services (infrastructure/IT support services) and C=Business services (services delivering business value). Application services are a separate CSDM classification; mobile services are not a standard SPM-managed service type.

questions.stem: Which is the process responsible for delivering items that have been ordered from a Service Catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Request Fulfillment: C=Catalog Fulfillment (Request Fulfillment) is the ITIL process responsible for delivering items ordered from the Service Catalog. Service Catalog Management governs the catalog lifecycle; Catalog Workflows, Catalog Item Design, and Request Management are related but not the fulfillment process name.

questions.stem: Where is the definition of what is provided, or not provided, for a service defined?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Service Scope: The B=Service scope defines what is provided and not provided for a service — its inclusions and exclusions. Vendor service agreements and service contracts are legal/commercial documents; service limitations is not a standard SPM term.

questions.stem: When using Catalog Builder, what can be built using templates? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder: Catalog Builder templates can be used to build B=Catalog items (standard fulfillment items) and E=Record producers (items that create records in other tables). Content Items, Knowledge articles, and Order Guides are not supported item types in Catalog Builder templates.

questions.stem: If a change model has Write roles AND Can write defined, which users have the ability to modify the change model record? (Choose two.)

options.text: Users that have the Write role(s) OR that match the Can write user criteria
Users that have the Write role(s) AND match the Can write user criteria

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Model Security (p353): When both Write roles AND Can write user criteria are defined, B=users with admin role always retain access, and E=users must have the Write role(s) AND match the Can write user criteria (both conditions must be met). itil_admin and sn_change_write alone are not sufficient when Can write criteria is also defined.

questions.stem: What defines the required approvals and the associated conditions for a change model?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Approval Policy (p1040): A=A change approval policy defines the required approvals and associated conditions (decisions) for a change model's flows. State transitions control movement between states; change model approval definition and change approval lifecycle flow are not standard ServiceNow component names.

questions.stem: Which organizational role is responsible for the overall administrative capabilities of a portfolio?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Roles: B=Portfolio Manager is the organizational role responsible for the overall administrative capabilities and governance of a service portfolio. Service Manager manages day-to-day services; Portfolio Owner is not a standard SPM role; Service Owner manages individual services, not the portfolio.

questions.stem: What defines which catalog items, and in what order, are included in an Order Guide?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Order Guide: B=Rules on an Order Guide define which catalog items are included in the guide and their display order. Order guide templates, variable sets, and UI policies do not control which items are included or their sequence.

questions.stem: A customer requires incidents to automatically move to a Closed state from Resolved after 7 days. How is this configured? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the incident lifecycle flow script action
Configure the number of days Resolved incidents automatically close property
Configure the incident lifecycle timeline property
Enable the auto closure of Incidents based on Resolution date property

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Incident Management > Auto-Close (p2475): To auto-close Resolved incidents after 7 days, B=configure the number of days in the Resolved incidents automatically close property (glide.ui.autoclose.time) and D=enable the auto closure of Incidents based on Resolution date property. Lifecycle flow scripts and timeline properties are not the correct configuration paths.

questions.stem: On the ‘Create New’ change landing page in Service Operations Workspace, what class label is displayed for the Emergency change model?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Create New Landing Page: On the SOW Create New change landing page, the Emergency change model displays with the C=Break/fix class label. Unauthorized, Default, and Out-of-the-box are not the class labels used for the Emergency model.

questions.stem: Which of these can be defined using step based fulfillment in Catalog Builder? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Catalog Builder > Step-Based Fulfillment: Using step-based fulfillment in Catalog Builder, you can define A=Approvals (approval steps) and D=Tasks (catalog tasks assigned to fulfillment teams). Subflow triggers, Notifications, and Payment processing are not available as step-based fulfillment components in Catalog Builder.

questions.stem: Which Service Portfolio Management phase does a service belong to when it is in operational state?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management (p1950): When a service is in operational state (Status=Operational), it belongs to the C=Catalog phase in Service Portfolio Management. The Catalog phase represents active, live services. Pipeline is for services in development; Active and Retired are not standard SPM phase names.

questions.stem: What is normally done when a Root Cause and a Workaround are identified for a problem to document the quickest known resolution?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Known Error Articles (p2860): When both root cause and workaround are identified, B=Document a Known Error by creating a Known Error article capturing both as the quickest known resolution. A Known Error is specifically a problem where both root cause and workaround are known; publishing a workaround alone does not formally document the root cause.

questions.stem: A Portfolio Manager is primarily concerned with the performance of what hierarchy?

options.text: Portfolio Owner, Service Owner, Catalog Manager
Service Catalog, Catalog item, Requested item
Requested Item, Catalog Task, Task SLA

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management: A Portfolio Manager is primarily concerned with the A=Service Portfolio, Service, Service Offering hierarchy — performance visibility from portfolio level down to individual offerings. The other options describe roles (B), catalog items (C), or fulfillment records (D).

questions.stem: When modifying a Change Flow, a library is available of re-usable components for your flow. What are these components called?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Change Flows (p486): The reusable components in the Change Flow library are B=Flow actions — pre-built, reusable automation components (e.g., Evaluate Change Model, Apply Change Approval Policy). Flow activities, Attributes, and Properties are not the correct Flow Designer terminology.

questions.stem: How is granular read and write access for a specific change model defined?

options.text: Configuring ACL's on the chge_model table
Configuring ACL's on the Create New landing page
Setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Model Security: Granular read and write access for a specific change model is defined by D=setting Advanced Security to true on the change model and applying user criteria, enabling role-based access controls restricting which users can create/read/update change requests using that model.

questions.stem: Which of the following can leverage user criteria for controlling access?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > User Criteria: E=Catalog items can leverage user criteria to control which users can view and order specific items. Catalog taxonomy, topics, categories, and variables are not the primary elements in the service catalog where user criteria controls access.

questions.stem: Which level are service commitments associated in the service portfolio taxonomy?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Commitments: Service commitments are associated at the B=Offering level — each service offering defines the commitment (availability, scope, pricing) for a specific tier of service. Taxonomy nodes, portfolios, and services are higher-level groupings that don't directly hold service commitments.

questions.stem: How are the relationships between services and offerings that are built in Service Portfolio Management transferred to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)?

options.text: Only parent:child (service:offering) relationships are automatically created in the CMDB
If the service is defined as a business service, the relationships and dependencies will be automatically in the CMDB
All CMDB relationships and dependencies are automatically created upon publishing the service and offerings
Any required CMDB relationships and dependencies must be created manually

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > CMDB Integration: C=All CMDB relationships and dependencies are automatically created when services and offerings are published in Service Portfolio Management. The SPM application maintains CMDB synchronization, eliminating the need for manual relationship creation.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of offering(s) a service must have to move to the Catalog phase?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Lifecycle: A service must have a minimum of A=1 offering to move to the Catalog phase and become available for ordering. Services without at least one offering cannot advance to the Catalog phase.

questions.stem: Your client indicates they would like a way to designate VIP callers on an incident form. How would you accomplish this?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > VIP Status (p2457): VIP callers are designated on the incident form using a D=Field style (VIP field decorator/style), which applies visual highlighting to indicate VIP status in list view and form. Dictionary entry attributes, Reference decorators, and Action scripts are not the mechanism for this.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the approvals that should be applied to a change request?
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Approval Policy (p282): A B=Change approval policy defines the approvals applied to a change request — it uses variable inputs to evaluate decisions, with each matching decision applying associated approval definitions. UI actions, script includes, and business rules are not the mechanism for defining change approvals.

questions.stem: What do you use to identify who will have access to particular items in a service catalog?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Access Control: A=User criteria is the mechanism used to identify which users have access to specific service catalog items. User criteria records define conditions based on user attributes, groups, or roles. Access criteria, User access rules, Availability rules, and Security rules are not ServiceNow catalog access control terms.

questions.stem: Once a Catalog Item has been requested, what mechanism determines the approvals, and tasks that are triggered in the application?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Request Management: Once a catalog item is requested, D=Flows (Flow Designer) determine the approvals and tasks triggered during fulfillment. "Request Management allows catalog items to be requested and fulfilled based on defined flows." Decision Tables, Actions, Run Books, and Playbooks are not the primary fulfillment mechanism.

questions.stem: What is a core difference between an Incident and a Problem?

options.text: Incidents are focused on one individual having an issue; Problems are when you have many people having the same issue
Incidents can be any priority; Problems are high or critical
Incidents are the same as a Problem
Incidents are focused on the quickest resolution; Problems are focused on root cause analysis

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > ITSM Process: The core difference is D=Incidents are focused on restoring service as quickly as possible (quickest resolution), while Problems are focused on root cause analysis to prevent recurrence. Incidents are not limited to individuals or specific priority levels; Problems and incidents are not the same.

questions.stem: Where can a change manager define the fields that must be populated before a change request can move from the state of New to Assess?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Change Management > Model State Transition Conditions (p352): Change managers define fields that must be populated before a change can transition between states (e.g., New to Assess) using B=Model State Transition Conditions. Choice conditions, Dictionary Overrides, and State choice lists do not control field population requirements for state transitions.

questions.stem: When building multiple catalog items, which components should be evaluated for consolidation and re-use? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Best Practices: When building multiple catalog items, B=Flows and Subflows can be consolidated for reuse across items sharing fulfillment logic, and C=Sets of variables (variable sets) can be shared across items with common input fields. Approvals are item-specific; Workflow Triggers are not a catalog reuse concept.

questions.stem:
Your company sells bicycles. They want to build a service catalog for current and prospective customers, so they can browse for bicycles and accessories, and make purchases.

What interface is suitable for these external users?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Interfaces: B=Portal (Service Portal) is the appropriate interface for external customer-facing catalogs, providing a branded self-service experience for browsing and ordering. Service Catalog Mobile App and Now Catalog App are internal IT interfaces; Google leads spoke and Customer Service Catalog are not standard ServiceNow interfaces.

questions.stem: By default, an Assignment group is automatically set on a change request record because of a business rule. How is the group identified?

options.text: Change group on CI record, or if empty, the Change group on the Service offering
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service
Support group on CI record, or the default assignment group for the user
Support group on CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service offering

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Auto-Assignment: The "Populate Assignment Group based on CI/SO" business rule identifies the assignment group as D=the Support group on the CI record, or if empty, the Support group on the Service Offering. Change group, the default user group, and Business Service fallbacks are not used in this rule.

questions.stem: What happens when an existing service record is checked out in service Builder for editing?

options.text: The service portfolio record is placed in a Work in progress state
The service and offerings are temporarily unavailable for consumption
A copy of the service is created and placed in a Draft state
The original service record is placed in a Retired state

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Service Builder (p2934): When an existing service record is checked out for editing, C=a copy of the service is automatically created and placed in Draft state for editing. The original published record remains active; the service portfolio is not moved to Work in Progress; the original is not retired.

questions.stem: Users with which role can Communicate a workaround or fix? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Communicate Roles (p2858): Users with C=problem_manager and D=problem_admin roles can Communicate workarounds and fixes. itil_admin is not a standard role; problem_task_analyst is a lower-level role focused on technical investigation without communication link permissions.

questions.stem: What tools are available to the assignee to help resolve an incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Resolution Assistance: A=Workarounds (from Known Error articles documenting workarounds for known issues) and B=Resolutions from similar incidents (Task Intelligence recommendations) are available to assignees. CI Class Manager, Enterprise CMDB Dashboard, and Incident Overview Dashboard are management/admin tools.

questions.stem: By default, when using Inbound actions, what happens if an email is received and has an Incident watermark?

options.text: Incident record is set to state = on hold
Incident record is updated, per the action's script
Auto-reply sent to sender, recommending they use Portal chat

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Incident Management > Inbound Email: When an inbound email contains an incident watermark, the default inbound action script C=updates the matched Incident record (e.g., adds a journal entry or reopens). The incident is not set to On Hold, the SLA clock is not paused, and no portal chat auto-reply is sent.

questions.stem: Which of the following can leverage user criteria for controlling access? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > User Criteria: C=Catalog categories and E=Catalog items can leverage user criteria to control which users can view and access them. Catalog taxonomy, topics, and variables are not elements where user criteria is applied for access control.

questions.stem: Which of the following is defined in the Assess Dialog Form View for problem records?

options.text: The notifications that are sent to Problem Analysts when a problem record is moved from the New to Assess state.
The text displayed in the dialog box when a problem record moves from the New to Assess state.
The users that receive notifications when a problem record is moved from the New to Assess state.
The fields which are required to be populated for the record to automatically move from the New to Assess state.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Problem Management > Assess Dialog (p2835): The Assess Dialog Form View for problem records defines D=the fields required to be populated for the record to automatically move from New to Assess state. It does not define notifications, the text of the dialog, or the notification recipients.

questions.stem: What role is required to accept a Major Incident?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Major Incident Management > Roles (p2509): The D=major_incident_manager role is required to accept a Major Incident (and perform MIM workbench actions). incident_admin, itil_admin, and incident_manager do not have the specific authority to accept a major incident candidate.

questions.stem: Which service type is published to service owners and typically only consumed internally?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] ITSM > Service Portfolio Management > Service Types (p3423): B=Technical service is the service type published to service owners and typically consumed internally (e.g., infrastructure services). Business services are published to business users; Mobile and Application service are not SPM-defined service types based on consumption pattern.

questions.stem: How is granular read and write access for a specific change model defined?

options.text: Configuring ACL's on the Create New landing page
Setting Advanced Security to true and applying user criteria
Configuring ACL’s on the chge_model table

questions.explanation: [Platform] ITSM > Change Management > Change Model Security: Granular read/write access for a specific change model is defined by B=setting Advanced Security to true on the change model and applying user criteria, enabling role/group-based controls. ACLs on the landing page or change_model table and Change properties do not provide per-model granular security.

questions.stem: In what part of the Request management lifecycle, does the user fill out the form for the item they are requesting?
questions.explanation: [Platform] Service Catalog > Request Lifecycle: In the Request Management lifecycle, the E=Input phase is when the user fills out the form for the item they are requesting. Submittal is order confirmation; Inquiry is awareness/browsing; Specification defines the item; Check out/checkout is completing the cart process.
